questions.skill: Construct a square on a given segment
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs. Construct a square with side AB, above AB.
questions.prompt_markup:
Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs.
Construct a square with side AB, above AB.
questions.correct_answer: Construct perpendiculars to AB at A and at B; copy AB onto each, on the SAME side of AB (above it), to get D and C; join C and D.
questions.grading_note: Grade the construction marks, not only the final figure: two perpendicular constructions and two segment copies on the same side of AB. Copies on opposite sides give a crossed figure, not a square.

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A square on segment AB is constructed by drawing perpendiculars to AB at A and at B and copying AB onto each, on the same side of line AB, to get D (from A) and C (from B). Explain why ABCD is a square, and why the two copies must be on the same side of AB.
questions.prompt_markup: A square on segment AB is constructed by drawing perpendiculars to AB at A and at B and copying AB onto each, on the same side of line AB, to get D (from A) and C (from B). Explain why ABCD is a square, and why the two copies must be on the same side of AB.
questions.correct_answer: AD ∥ BC (both ⊥ AB) and AD = BC, so ABCD is a parallelogram; it has a right angle at A, so it is a rectangle; AB = AD, so all sides are equal: a square. If D and C were on opposite sides, segment DC would cross AB and ABCD would not be a quadrilateral with these sides.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation with both parts.
